**Observation Log:**

- [FACT] The user is interested in developing a lesson plan for upper-level college students.
- [ASSISTANT_CREATED] The assistant created a lesson plan titled "Identifying and Developing Story Ideas for Print and Online Publications."
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The objective of the lesson is for students to be able to identify and develop story ideas for print and online publications by the end of the lesson.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Materials needed for the lesson include handouts on brainstorming techniques and story idea development, writing prompts, and access to current news and publications.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The introduction of the lesson is scheduled for 10 minutes and will review the importance of finding and developing story ideas for print and online publications.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The role of a journalist in identifying and reporting on relevant and interesting stories will be discussed during the introduction.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The brainstorming techniques section is planned for 15 minutes, where students will practice different methods in small groups using handouts provided.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Students are encouraged to think outside of the box and consider different perspectives during the brainstorming techniques section.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The writing prompts section is allocated 20 minutes, where students will receive a list of prompts related to current events to develop potential story ideas.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Students are encouraged to think about the angle and focus of each story during the writing prompts section.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The research and development section is planned for 40 minutes, where students will research current news and publications for inspiration.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Students will have access to a variety of sources, including newspapers, magazines, and online news websites during the research and development section.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Students are expected to develop one or two story ideas they find interesting, including an angle and a focus.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The sharing and feedback section is scheduled for 20 minutes, where students will share their developed story ideas with the class.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Students will provide feedback on each other's ideas and think about how to pitch their story to an editor or publication during the sharing and feedback section.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The conclusion of the lesson is set for 10 minutes, summarizing the importance of finding and developing story ideas.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The skills learned in this lesson will be discussed in terms of their application to future writing and journalism assignments.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Assessment will include students turning in a written proposal for one of the story ideas developed during class.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Students will participate in class discussions and provide feedback on their peers' story ideas
